predecessors.name: igodomigodo
predecessors.text: the previous Edo Kingdom of Igodomigodo (Ogiso rule), from which the Benin kingdom grew

successors.name: Niger Coast Protectorate
successors.text: Benin was absorbed into the British Niger Coast Protectorate after Benin City fell on 18 February 1897

ledger.x: 1180: the Edo city-state under its Oba.
1440: Ewuare the Great begins the conquests.
ledger.cp: Akure, Owo and the Ekiti town-states

ledger.x: 1440: Ewuare takes the western Igbo, Ika and Kukuruku villages.
1517: Esigie beats the Igala and extends Benin east and south.
ledger.cp: Delta peoples (Urhobo, Isoko, Ijaw and western Igbo)

ledger.x: 1600: the warrior kings end and the empire shrinks.
ledger.cp: Delta peoples (Urhobo, Isoko, Ijaw and western Igbo)

ledger.x: c. 1630: Eko (Lagos) is a tributary of Benin. 'The Oba of Benin appointed him [Ashipa] as ruler of Eko'; Ashipa 'initiated a payment of tribute that would not be abolished until 1830'; the Oba of Lagos list has Ashipa 1600-1630 ('not crowned') and Ado, first crowned king, from 1630. Reviewer…

c. 1830: Lagos stops paying tribute to Benin: tribute 'would not be abolished until 1830'; 'Eko's subservience to Benin was mostly nominal by the 18th century'. Reviewer af-04-x (2026-10-19): added as the mirror of kingdom-of-lagos 1830.
1897 (18 February): the kingdom passes to the British.

1897 (February): the Benin Empire ends with the fall of Benin City; Oba Ovonramwen died in exile at Calabar in January 1914 and his son was enthroned as Eweka II on 24 July 1914, who 'rebuilt the royal palace, which had been destroyed in 1897'.

wars.name: Benin-Igala war of Esigie
wars.outcome: Benin defeated the Igala invasion; 'the victory altered Benin's relationship with Idah and reinforced the Oba's influence in the Niger region' (Ryder, via the Esigie page).

wars.name: Benin civil war
wars.outcome: Civil war 'around 1689, around the time that Oba Ewuakpe ascended'; it lasted about ten years before negotiations, and Akenzua's side 'eventually prevailed over the younger Ozuere and his ally, the Iyase Ode in a decisive battle in 1721'; about ten more years…

wars.name: British Benin Expedition
wars.outcome: British victory: 1,200 troops under Sir Harry Rawson captured Benin City on 18 February 1897; the kingdom was absorbed into the Niger Coast Protectorate; a Benin Territories Expedition in 1899 cleared holdouts.

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier line for the kingdom; the extents are the researcher's reading of lists of conquered towns and peoples.
